Summary: Python String Concatenation Performance Profile I've profiled and optimized the O(n²) string concatenation code. Here's what I found: 🐛 The Bottleneck Root Cause: Python strings are immutable. When you use += in a loop: [code] Each iteration: - Allocates new memory for len(result) + len("text") - Copies the entire existing string - Copies the new text - Frees old memory This creates O(n²) time complexity - for n concatenations, it does 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n copies = n(n+1)/2 operations. ⚡ Optimized Solutions (All O(n)) 📊 Benchmark Results [code] 📝 Best Practice [code] Files Created - slow_code.py - Original O(n²) code - optimized_code.py - 5 optimized versions - profile_code.py - cProfiler profiling - benchmark.py - Performance comparisons - detailed_benchmark.py - Detailed analysis with best practices - profiling_summary.md - Full documentation

Here's what I found: 🐛 The Bottleneck Root Cause: Python strings are immutable.
